---
title: "Before you come"
---

Please complete these steps at home. The wifi in the room may be slow, so download and install everything before the day. The whole setup takes about 15 minutes, and most of that is the package installation.

## What to bring

- **A laptop** on which you can install software. That is all you need.

**Optional.** If you have a dataset of your own, you are welcome to bring it, but nothing in the session uses it. Everything we run uses the TIMSS data in the repository. The last block of the Chapter 5 page is a template for pointing the code at your data after the session, and it expects one row per individual, a 0/1 treatment column, a site or cluster identifier, a few covariates, and an outcome.

## What to install

1. **R.** Install R 4.3 or later from <https://cran.r-project.org>.

2. **RStudio or Positron.** Either one. Both include Quarto, which you need only if you want to render the documents rather than run the chunks.

3. **This repository.** Download the zip file from the green Code button at <https://github.com/alberto-guzman/multilevel-matching-workshop>, or clone it. Unzip it. In RStudio, open `multilevel-matching-workshop.Rproj`. In Positron, open the folder. Either way, the working directory is then the repository, which the scripts assume.

4. **The packages.** Open `00_install_packages.R` and run it. It installs 15 packages from CRAN. If R asks whether to install a package from source, answer no.

5. **The setup check.** Open `00_check_setup.R` and run it. The last line should read `MatchIt test run: matched 710 students`. Two other lines are fine and need no action, a `FALSE` on the Quarto line and a note reading `Registered S3 method overwritten by 'car'`. If the script reports a missing package or an error, bring the output with you and we will fix it at the start of the session.

Download the zip even if you plan to follow along on this site, because the pages are large.

## What to know

- Basic R, meaning running a script, reading a data frame, and using the pipe. The code uses the tidyverse verbs `filter`, `mutate`, and `summarise` throughout.
- Nothing else in advance. The first hour of the workshop covers the ideas the code relies on, which are potential outcomes, the propensity score, and the standardized mean difference.

## If the installation fails

You can still follow along. Every output in every document is on this site, so you can watch on screen without running anything, fix the installation afterwards, and run the documents at home.
